column1: # Known deviations of upstream versions, for scripts/smoke.sh and scripts/interop.sh.
# Adapters are published on the latest upstream release even when it has a bug;
# the bug is listed here (and in docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) instead of pinning an
# older release. The same entries apply to candidate builds, so that one
# upstream bug is reported as such instead of hiding whether everything else
# works. An entry only applies to the version it names: on any other version the
# case fails and someone decides again.
# A case an entry covers counts as a known difference only when the document also
# matches the signature of that deviation; anything else is a failure. A deviation
# that no longer shows fails the run; remove its line then.
#   1  adapter     the stack with the deviation
#   5  cases       regex over the case id, without the suite
#   6  signature   jq filter on the result document
#   7  on-pass     "stale": a run in which it never shows fails.
#                  "may-pass": it depends on timing, a pass is fine too.
#   9  waiver      stable waiver id of results.json

column8: A None/None session of the open62541 client is refused: the server answers ActivateSession with a null ServerNonce (Part 4 5.6.3.2 asks for at least 32 bytes), which open62541 rejects. Over a secured channel the nonce is 32 bytes and the pair interoperates (tests/secure-cases.tsv).

Responses keep the token of their request across a SecureChannel renewal (Part 6 6.7.4: the server switches once it receives a message with the new token). Once the old token's lifetime has passed the open62541 client drops such a response and the subscription stalls; whether a late response lands after the expiry depends on publish timing.
The client compares the CreateSession server certificate with the leaf byte for byte, so it does not take a server that sends its chain (docs/CONTAINER_CONTRACT.md 16.3).

A percent deadband on a node without EURange is accepted: MonitoredItemService logs that it is not implemented and reports every change, instead of BadMonitoredItemFilterUnsupported or BadFilterNotAllowed.
HistoryUpdate is refused: the permission ruleset denies it for the User role the adapter gives every session, and the dispatcher has no handler behind it.

A Value the AccessLevel does not allow is refused with BadUserAccessDenied, on reading and on writing: both checks test the user access level alone. BadNotReadable and BadNotWritable are the status codes for this, and docs/FIXTURES.md asks for them.

A Value the AccessLevel does not allow is refused with BadUserAccessDenied, on reading and on writing: DefaultAccessController tests the user access level and answers DENIED_USER_ACCESS. BadNotReadable and BadNotWritable are the status codes for this, and docs/FIXTURES.md asks for them.

A Value the AccessLevel does not allow is refused with BadUserAccessDenied, on reading and on writing: is_readable and is_writable test the user access level alone. BadNotReadable and BadNotWritable are the status codes for this, and docs/FIXTURES.md asks for them.
Writing a Value the AccessLevel does not allow answers BadUserAccessDenied, not BadNotWritable. Reading answers BadNotReadable.

A released history continuation point stays valid: the adapter checks a set of released points that it never fills, because the HistoryRead handler does not see the release. An adapter defect, not one of Milo.
NumValuesPerNode cuts the result without a continuation point: the rest of the samples cannot be read. The history storage only returns a point for its own response limit.

column6: .success == true and (.results[0].events | length) == 2 and .results[0].events[0].fields[4].value == 500 and .results[0].events[0].fields[3].value == null
column8: The event-subscribe of the adapter prints strings and numbers only: EventId, EventType, Message and Time come out as null with every server (docs/CONTAINER_CONTRACT.md asks for them). An adapter defect.
Deleting an event that does not exist answers BadNoData for that operation, not BadNoEntryExists like every other stack (docs/CONTAINER_CONTRACT.md 17 records it).

With a trust list, CreateSession also checks the client certificate of a session without security, which Part 4 5.6.2 tells the server to ignore. The node-opcua client sends its generated certificate there and is refused.

The UserTokenPolicies of the opc.https and opc.wss endpoints name no security policy, so a password goes unencrypted inside TLS. The server cannot be told otherwise, and the UA-.NETStandard client refuses to send it.
